 Applications Open for 2 State Loan Forgiveness Programs
 Posted on November 20, 2026, 10:57 am Author Pam Robinson Leave a comment 
 Applications are open for two New York State student loan forgiveness programs aimed at strengthening the state’s health care and agricultural workforces while helping New Yorkers reduce their student loan debt.
 The  Nursing Faculty Loan Forgiveness Incentive Program, open to applicants eligible for the 2025 program year and the Young Farmers Loan Forgiveness Incentive Program , open for the 2026 program year, provide eligible applicants with up to $40,000 and $50,000 in student loan forgiveness, respectively. Applications for both programs close Dec.16, 2026.
 Administered by the[ New York State Higher Education Services Corporation, the programs encourage qualified professionals to pursue careers that are essential to New York’s communities and economy. Both programs combined have $2.1 million available to help nursing educators and young farmers with education debt while continuing to serve New Yorkers.
 “From the nurses who train our future health care professionals to the farmers who help feed our families, New York depends on people who dedicate their careers to serving others,” Gov. Kathy Hochul said.“Student debt shouldn’t stand in the way of their careers, and that’s what these loan forgiveness programs are all about. We’re investing in the people and industries that keep our communities strong, which is why I encourage eligible New Yorkers to apply and build their futures here in New York.”
 The Nursing Faculty Loan Forgiveness Incentive Program is designed to increase the number of qualified nursing faculty and adjunct clinical faculty teaching at nursing schools across the state. By helping nursing educators repay their student loans, the program supports efforts to prepare the next generation of nurses and strengthen the state’s health care workforce.
 Eligible recipients may receive up to $8,000 annually in student loan forgiveness for up to five years, with a maximum lifetime award of $40,000.
 To qualify, applicants must meet eligibility requirements, including: Be a registered nurse professionally licensed to practice in New York State.
 Possess a master’s degree in nursing or a doctoral degree qualifying them to serve as nursing faculty or adjunct clinical faculty.
 Have prior clinical experience as a licensed registered nurse.
 Be employed as nursing faculty or adjunct clinical faculty at a nursing school in New York State, providing classroom or clinical instruction equivalent to at least 12 credit hours annually.
 Have outstanding eligible student loan debt incurred while obtaining a nursing degree.
 Meet other program eligibility requirements.
 The Young Farmers Loan Forgiveness Incentive Program helps college graduates pursue long-term careers in agriculture by reducing the financial burden of student loan debt. The program supports New York’s agricultural workforce by encouraging graduates to establish and maintain full-time farming operations in the state.
 Eligible recipients may receive up to $10,000 annually in student loan forgiveness for up to five years, with a maximum lifetime award of $50,000.
 To qualify, applicants must meet several requirements, including: Have earned an undergraduate degree from an approved New York State college or university.
 Be within their first 10 years of operating a farm in New York State that produces agricultural products.
 Operate a farm in New York State on a full-time basis and agree to continue doing so for at least five years.
 Have outstanding eligible student loan debt associated with obtaining their undergraduate degree.
 Meet other program eligibility requirements.
